correctness.rationale: With Fourier convention exp(-2 pi i t xi), the Poisson transform is (pi/w)exp(-2 pi w|xi|). Two geometric series give the exact Zak symbol. Parseval in integer redundant lattice yields precisely sum_{j=0}^{q-1}|Zg(x,omega+j/q)|^2, including multiplicity. Every term is strictly increasing in cos(2 pi x); frequency optimization reduces to a finite hyperbolic sum with unique extremal phases. The resulting exact formula has positive A for every q>=2. The torus symbol is continuous, hence its connected image is the entire frame spectrum. For q=2, the condition-number derivative has a quartic that becomes 4t^4+6t^3-2t^2-5t-2 on t>0; one Descartes sign change plus endpoint signs proves a unique critical point/minimizer. A replayed standalone check ran 951 deterministic assertions. Numerical testing alone proves no infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: The new sharp-constant portion concerns every integer q>=3 for the even Poisson window, plus the explicitly optimized q=2 width as a corollary. An accessible historical claim for two staggered time-translation cosets with integer modulations already implies the q=2 bounds by unitary dilation, so q=2 sharp constants are not novel and are not counted toward O. The same earlier statement does not cover the q>=3 frequency-oversampled family. Belov–Semenov proves qualitative frame status; generic Janssen/Zak machinery does not evaluate the Poisson symbol at all q. The inaccessible 1996 Janssen complete text remains the material originality risk.
residual_risks: Janssen (1996), full text not accessible: its abstract concerns several unspecified windows and exact integer-redundancy frame bounds, so implicit direct coverage cannot be excluded.
Unindexed or unpublished explicit Poisson-window frame-bound evaluations may exist.
Publicly indexed record summaries cannot rule out stronger theorems hidden in uninspected complete articles.
The q=2 constants are derivable from a previously obtained staggered-time result, so they do not independently establish originality; originality rests on the q>=3 all-integer family.

value.rationale: The quantitative frame problem for Poisson windows is natural. The new sharp bounds for every integer q>=3 form an unbounded family of exact frequency-oversampled stability constants and full frame spectra not supplied by a qualitative frame criterion or a prior two-coset result. The calculation requires a Poisson-specific Zak symbol, global monotonicity and a finite hyperbolic-sum optimization. The q=2 optimal width is useful but is explicitly distinguished from the already-covered q=2 frame constants. The result is not an arbitrary cutoff or merely a finite computation.
